section.p: Consider a .docx document where the author has populated the document properties (File → Info → Properties) with Author, Created date, Last Modified date, Keywords, Company, and Subject values, with no field codes present in the body.

row.entry: [Document Properties] Title: Configuring Network Settings Author: XYZ Created date: 2025-03-14 Last Modified date: 2025-11-02 Keywords: network, configuration, setup Company: ABC Corp Subject: Device network setup

entry.codeblock: <concept id="configuring_network_settings"> <title>Configuring Network Settings</title> <prolog> <author>XYZ</author> <critdates> <created date="2025-03-14"/> <revised modified="2025-11-02"/> </critdates> <metadata> <keywords> <keyword>network</keyword> <keyword>configuration</keyword> <keyword>setup</keyword> </keywords> <othermeta name="company" content="ABC Corp"/> <othermeta name="subject" content="Device network setup"/> </metadata> </prolog> <conbody> ... </conbody> </concept>

section.p: Result: Each populated document property is mapped to its corresponding DITA <prolog> element — Author maps to <author>, Created date and Last Modified date map to <critdates><created> and <critdates><revised>, and Keywords maps to a list of <keyword> elements inside <metadata>. Company and Subject map to <othermeta name="company"> and <othermeta name="subject"> since neither has a dedicated DITA prolog element. The Title property supplies the topic title.
